root_cause.text: The bcmgenet_timeout handler incorrectly resets and restarts all TX queues when only a single queue times out, causing race conditions with other queues that are still active.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states the handler "tries to take down all tx queues when a single queue times out" and "causes many race conditions with queues that are still chugging along." The patch changes the logic from looping over all queues (bcmgenet_dump_tx_queue, bcmgenet_tx_reclaim_all, bcmgenet_intrl2_1_writel with all queue bits, netif_tx_wake_all_queues) to operating only on the specific timed-out queue (ring = &priv->tx_rings[txqueue], bcmgenet_tx_reclaim(dev, ring, true), re-enabling only 1 << txqueue, netif_tx_wake_queue(txq)).

intent_record.intent_summary: Scope timeout handling to the specific TX queue that triggered the timeout instead of processing all queues.
intent_record.what: Changed bcmgenet_timeout to operate only on the specific TX queue that triggered the timeout, replacing loops over all queues with targeted per-queue operations.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the timeout handler now dumps, reclaims, re-enables interrupts, updates transmission timestamp, increments error count, and wakes only the queue indicated by txqueue, rather than all queues.

grouping_result.intent: Scope timeout handling to the specific TX queue that triggered the timeout instead of processing all queues.

relevance_review.reason: The group fixes the vulnerability by scoping timeout handling to the specific TX queue that timed out, which directly addresses the root cause of resetting all queues and causing race conditions.
